### 2b. `dot_zlogin.tmpl` (new)

Chezmoi `dot_zlogin.tmpl` becomes `~/.zlogin`. Zsh sources `.zlogin` only on **login shells**, which is exactly what fresh SSH sessions get; subsequent shells inside that SSH session (subshells, tmux panes) do not re-trigger it. This is the right hook — better than `.zshrc`.

```sh
# ~/.zlogin - login-shell hooks (managed by chezmoi)
# Prints an SSH-only MOTD banner. Local terminals get nothing.

# Gate 1: only on SSH login (covers ssh, sftp interactive — but sftp uses
# .zshenv, so this is effectively the SSH shell case).
[ -n "$SSH_CONNECTION" ] || return 0

# Gate 2: only if stdout is a TTY. Filters out `ssh host 'cmd'` non-interactive
# invocations and scp/rsync sub-shells.
[ -t 1 ] || return 0

# Gate 3: respect an opt-out env var the user can set in ~/.zshrc.adhoc
[ "${MOTD_DISABLE:-0}" = "1" ] && return 0

# --- Banner -----------------------------------------------------------------
_motd_host="$(hostname -s 2>/dev/null || hostname)"
_motd_cols="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 80)}"

# Cyan for figlet, dim for metadata. No lolcat dependency: lolcat stays a
# user-facing utility (`echo hi | lolcat`), not a banner runtime dep.
printf '\033[36m'
if command -v figlet >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # -w respects terminal width; -f small keeps tall hostnames readable
    figlet -w "$_motd_cols" -f small -- "$_motd_host" 2>/dev/null \
        || figlet -w "$_motd_cols" -- "$_motd_host" 2>/dev/null \
        || printf '== %s ==\n' "$_motd_host"
else
    # First-boot fallback (figlet not yet installed by ansible)
    printf '== %s ==\n' "$_motd_host"
fi
printf '\033[0m'

# --- Metadata line ----------------------------------------------------------
{{- /* chezmoi-templated profile is baked in at apply time */ }}
_motd_profile='{{ .profile }}'
_motd_os="$(uname -sr)"
_motd_up="$(uptime 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*up *([^,]+),.*/\1/' | xargs)"
_motd_ip="$(echo "$SSH_CONNECTION" | awk '{print $3}')"  # server-side IP

printf '\033[2m'  # dim
printf 'profile=%s  os=%s  up=%s  via=%s\n' \
    "$_motd_profile" "$_motd_os" "${_motd_up:-?}" "${_motd_ip:-?}"
printf '\033[0m\n'

unset _motd_host _motd_cols _motd_profile _motd_os _motd_up _motd_ip
```

Rationale on each gate / line:
- **Login shell**: no need for an explicit `[[ -o login ]]` check — `.zlogin` only runs for login shells by definition, so we get that for free.
- **`hostname -s`**: short hostname (no FQDN). Cleaner banner.
- **`figlet -w "$_motd_cols"`**: handles long hostname overflow — figlet wraps to width.
- **Profile from chezmoi template**: baked at apply time, no runtime cost, no parsing.
- **`SSH_CONNECTION` field 3** = server-side IP (the address you SSH'd into) — useful for fleet identification when servers have multi-homed interfaces.
- **No lolcat**: keeps the banner deterministic (color piping breaks easily over flaky SSH; ANSI is bulletproof) and removes a hard dep on lolcat being installed.

### 2c. `README.md`

Append three names to the existing devtools listing line. Add (or graft into existing zsh section) a one-paragraph note:

> **SSH MOTD**: A short login-shell banner (`figlet $(hostname -s)` + profile/OS/uptime/IP) prints when you SSH into a host. Local terminals are silent. Set `MOTD_DISABLE=1` in `~/.zshrc.adhoc` to suppress it. See `docs/zsh/motd.md`.

### 2d. `docs/zsh/motd.md` (new, optional)

Brief doc page covering: trigger conditions, opt-out, how to customize hostname formatting, what happens before figlet is installed, and pointer to `dot_zlogin.tmpl`. Add to `mkdocs.yml` nav under `Zsh` if that section exists (verify before adding).

## 3. Decision: chezmoi prompt or not?

**No prompt.** Reasoning, point by point:

1. **Cost is trivial**: figlet+toilet+lolcat together are <1 MB installed. The chezmoi prompt list is already long (the user's own `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` comment says *"not all the things we want to change all the time we chezmoi init"*). Adding a prompt for sub-MB tooling violates the spirit of that note.
2. **The MOTD is already self-gating**: it only fires on SSH + TTY. Users who never SSH never see it. There's nothing to "opt out" of at install time.
3. **Runtime opt-out exists**: `MOTD_DISABLE=1` covers the rare "I SSH in but hate banners" case without polluting init UX.
4. **No new profile values**: stays within the existing `macos` / `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server` set.
5. **Consistency precedent**: `bat`, `eza`, `tmux`, `glow`, `gum` etc. all install unconditionally via `devtools` without prompts. Banner tools belong in the same default-on bucket.

If the user later disagrees, the 3-file change is mechanical (key `installBannerTools`, ARG `CHEZMOI_INSTALL_BANNER_TOOLS`, `Prompt("installBannerTools", "bool", "Dev tooling", ...)` entry, and wrap the new ansible tasks in `when: installBannerTools | default(true)`). But shipping it default-on is the right call now.

## 6. Edge cases & how the design handles them

| Edge case | Handling |
|---|---|
| User SSHs in before ansible has installed figlet | `command -v figlet` check + `printf '== %s ==\n'` plain fallback. Banner still identifies host. |
| Long hostname overflowing terminal width | `figlet -w "$_motd_cols"` honors current `$COLUMNS` / `tput cols`. |
| Non-interactive SSH (`ssh host 'cmd'`) | `[ -t 1 ]` returns false → early return 0. No noise in scp/rsync/ansible runs. |
| tmux/screen attached **inside** an SSH session | First SSH login triggers `.zlogin` once → banner prints. Subsequent tmux panes don't re-source `.zlogin` (interactive non-login shells), so no spam. Correct behavior. |
| `tmux attach` reconnect to a session whose original shell was over SSH | New attach doesn't re-run `.zlogin` (it's a window in an existing process). No banner. Correct. |
| User logs in from console TTY (not SSH) | `$SSH_CONNECTION` empty → return 0. No banner. |
| `bash` user instead of zsh | `.zlogin` is zsh-specific. Bash users won't see the banner; that's acceptable since this repo is zsh-first (`dot_zshrc.tmpl`, no bash equivalents tracked). |
| User wants to disable | `export MOTD_DISABLE=1` in `~/.zshrc.adhoc` (file already auto-created by `dot_zshrc.tmpl` line 105). |
| `hostname -s` not present on some BSDs | Fallback chain: `hostname -s 2>/dev/null || hostname`. Linux+macOS both support `-s`. |
| ANSI codes in a non-color terminal | `\033[36m` / `\033[0m` are universally interpreted; worst case, a dumb terminal shows raw escapes — but `[ -t 1 ]` already filters most of those, and modern SSH terminals all support ANSI. |

## 7. Non-goals (explicit)

- **Not modifying** `dot_ansible/callback_plugins/clean.py`. Out of scope.
- **Not adding** banners to any `run_once_*` / `run_before_*` chezmoi script. Out of scope.
- **Not adding** `cowsay`, `boxes`, `fortune`, `fastfetch`, `neofetch`. Tight scope per CLAUDE.md.
- **Not adding** lolcat into the MOTD itself — lolcat stays an interactive user utility.
- **Not adding** a chezmoi init prompt. Default-on, runtime-gated.
- **Not adding** a bash equivalent (`/etc/motd`, `~/.bash_profile`). Repo is zsh-first.
- **Not adding** the banner to local (non-SSH) shells. The user's stated benefit is fleet identification.

# Plan: ASCII Banner Tools + SSH-Aware MOTD

## Context

User wants to install the figlet family of ASCII-banner CLI tools (`figlet`, `toilet`, `lolcat`) and configure a `~/.zlogin` MOTD that prints a big hostname banner — primarily so SSH'ing across the fleet of machines (managed via `fleet-apply`) makes "which box am I on?" obvious.

The discussion already established three things:
- Tools are tiny (<1MB total), universally packaged on apt + brew, no GitHub-release fallback needed.
- MOTD's real benefit is **SSH-only fleet identification**; local terminals don't need it.
- `clean.py` ansible callback and chezmoi `run_*` scripts are explicitly **out of scope** — they already have well-tuned output.

The user asked whether a chezmoi init prompt is needed. **Decision: not needed** (justified below).

## Scope

**In:**
1. Install `figlet`, `toilet`, `lolcat` via `devtools` ansible role (macOS Homebrew + Linux apt).
2. Create `dot_zlogin.tmpl` — SSH+TTY-gated banner with chezmoi-baked profile metadata.
3. Light README mention; optional `docs/zsh/motd.md` page.

**Out:**
- `cowsay`, `boxes`, `fortune`, `fastfetch`, `neofetch` — keep scope tight.
- chezmoi init prompt — runtime gating already covers all needed cases.
- `clean.py`, run-scripts, Brewfile.
- bash equivalent — repo is zsh-first.

## Files to modify / create

| Path | Action |
|---|---|
| `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` | modify — append 3 names to macOS list (line 55), add new apt task block at end of file, update tools comment on line 3 |
| `dot_zlogin.tmpl` | **create** new file at repo root |
| `README.md` | small touch — add 3 names + 1-paragraph "SSH MOTD" note |
| `docs/zsh/motd.md` + `mkdocs.yml` nav | optional but recommended — 1-page doc explaining trigger conditions and opt-out |

NOT touched: `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`, `Dockerfile`, `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py`, Brewfile, `clean.py`, any run-script.

## Implementation

### 1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`

# =============================================================================

### 2. `dot_zlogin.tmpl` (new file, repo root)

\```sh
# ~/.zlogin - login-shell hooks (managed by chezmoi)
# Prints an SSH-only MOTD banner. Local terminals get nothing.

# Gate 1: only on SSH login
[ -n "$SSH_CONNECTION" ] || return 0

# Gate 2: only if stdout is a TTY (filters `ssh host 'cmd'` and scp/rsync)
[ -t 1 ] || return 0

# Gate 3: don't repaint inside tmux (only the original SSH login shell prints)
[ -z "$TMUX" ] || return 0

# Gate 4: respect runtime opt-out from ~/.zshrc.adhoc
[ "${MOTD_DISABLE:-0}" = "1" ] && return 0

_motd_host="$(hostname -s 2>/dev/null || hostname)"
_motd_cols="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 80)}"

# Cyan banner. No lolcat dep at runtime — lolcat stays a user utility.
printf '\033[36m'
if command -v figlet >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    figlet -w "$_motd_cols" -f small -- "$_motd_host" 2>/dev/null \
        || figlet -w "$_motd_cols" -- "$_motd_host" 2>/dev/null \
        || printf '== %s ==\n' "$_motd_host"
else
    # Fallback for first-boot before ansible has installed figlet
    printf '== %s ==\n' "$_motd_host"
fi
printf '\033[0m'

# Metadata line — profile baked at chezmoi-apply time (zero runtime cost)
_motd_profile='{{ .profile }}'
_motd_os="$(uname -sr)"
_motd_up="$(uptime 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*up *([^,]+),.*/\1/' | xargs)"
_motd_ip="$(echo "$SSH_CONNECTION" | awk '{print $3}')"  # server-side IP

printf '\033[2m'
printf 'profile=%s  os=%s  up=%s  via=%s\n' \
    "$_motd_profile" "$_motd_os" "${_motd_up:-?}" "${_motd_ip:-?}"
printf '\033[0m\n'

unset _motd_host _motd_cols _motd_profile _motd_os _motd_up _motd_ip
\```

**Why each gate:**
- `SSH_CONNECTION` — the core trigger. Empty on console/local terminals.
- `[ -t 1 ]` — non-interactive SSH (e.g., `ssh host 'echo'`, scp, rsync, fleet-apply itself) returns false → silent. Also note: zsh `-c` non-interactive doesn't run `.zlogin` anyway, so this is belt-and-suspenders.
- `[ -z "$TMUX" ]` — handles the rare config where tmux spawns login shells; banner stays a once-per-SSH-session event.

2. **MOTD self-gates at runtime** — only fires on SSH+TTY+non-tmux. Users who never SSH never see it; nothing to opt out of at install time.

# Plan: ASCII Banner Tools + SSH-Aware MOTD

## Context

User wants to install the figlet family of ASCII-banner CLI tools (`figlet`, `toilet`, `lolcat`) and configure a `~/.zlogin` MOTD that prints a big hostname banner — primarily so SSH'ing across the fleet of machines (managed via `fleet-apply`) makes "which box am I on?" obvious.

The discussion already established three things:
- Tools are tiny (<1MB total), universally packaged on apt + brew, no GitHub-release fallback needed.
- MOTD's real benefit is **SSH-only fleet identification**; local terminals don't need it.
- `clean.py` ansible callback and chezmoi `run_*` scripts are explicitly **out of scope** — they already have well-tuned output.

The user asked whether a chezmoi init prompt is needed. **Decision: not needed** (justified below).

## Scope

**In:**
1. Install `figlet`, `toilet`, `lolcat` via `devtools` ansible role (macOS Homebrew + Linux apt).
2. Create `dot_zlogin.tmpl` — SSH+TTY-gated banner with chezmoi-baked profile metadata.
3. Light README mention; optional `docs/zsh/motd.md` page.

**Out:**
- `cowsay`, `boxes`, `fortune`, `fastfetch`, `neofetch` — keep scope tight.
- chezmoi init prompt — runtime gating already covers all needed cases.
- `clean.py`, run-scripts, Brewfile.
- bash equivalent — repo is zsh-first.

### 2. `dot_zlogin.tmpl` (new file, repo root)

```sh
# ~/.zlogin - login-shell hooks (managed by chezmoi)
# Prints an SSH-only MOTD banner. Local terminals get nothing.

# Gate 1: only on SSH login
[ -n "$SSH_CONNECTION" ] || return 0

# Gate 2: only if stdout is a TTY (filters `ssh host 'cmd'` and scp/rsync)
[ -t 1 ] || return 0

# Gate 3: don't repaint inside tmux (only the original SSH login shell prints)
[ -z "$TMUX" ] || return 0

# Gate 4: respect runtime opt-out from ~/.zshrc.adhoc
[ "${MOTD_DISABLE:-0}" = "1" ] && return 0

_motd_host="$(hostname -s 2>/dev/null || hostname)"
_motd_cols="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 80)}"

# Cyan banner. No lolcat dep at runtime — lolcat stays a user utility.
printf '\033[36m'
if command -v figlet >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    figlet -w "$_motd_cols" -f small -- "$_motd_host" 2>/dev/null \
        || figlet -w "$_motd_cols" -- "$_motd_host" 2>/dev/null \
        || printf '== %s ==\n' "$_motd_host"
else
    # Fallback for first-boot before ansible has installed figlet
    printf '== %s ==\n' "$_motd_host"
fi
printf '\033[0m'

# Metadata line — profile baked at chezmoi-apply time (zero runtime cost)
_motd_profile='{{ .profile }}'
_motd_os="$(uname -sr)"
_motd_up="$(uptime 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*up *([^,]+),.*/\1/' | xargs)"
_motd_ip="$(echo "$SSH_CONNECTION" | awk '{print $3}')"  # server-side IP

printf '\033[2m'
printf 'profile=%s  os=%s  up=%s  via=%s\n' \
    "$_motd_profile" "$_motd_os" "${_motd_up:-?}" "${_motd_ip:-?}"
printf '\033[0m\n'

unset _motd_host _motd_cols _motd_profile _motd_os _motd_up _motd_ip
```

**Why each gate:**
- `SSH_CONNECTION` — the core trigger. Empty on console/local terminals.
- `[ -t 1 ]` — non-interactive SSH (e.g., `ssh host 'echo'`, scp, rsync, fleet-apply itself) returns false → silent. Also note: zsh `-c` non-interactive doesn't run `.zlogin` anyway, so this is belt-and-suspenders.
- `[ -z "$TMUX" ]` — handles the rare config where tmux spawns login shells; banner stays a once-per-SSH-session event.
- `MOTD_DISABLE=1` — taste-based opt-out via `~/.zshrc.adhoc` (auto-created by `dot_zshrc.tmpl` line 104-122; perfect home for personal toggles).

99	### After install
100	
101	- `~/.local/bin` is auto-appended to `~/.bashrc` so `chezmoi`, `uv`, and `mise` stay reachable from bash.
102	- On sudo-enabled machines, the ansible `zsh` role switches your login shell to zsh automatically. Log out / back in to pick it up, or run `exec zsh` now.
103	- On `noRoot=true` installs, login shell isn't changed — run `exec zsh` per session, or ask your sysadmin: `sudo chsh -s "$(command -v zsh)" $USER`.
104	- Open a new shell (or `source ~/.bashrc`) after install so PATH changes take effect.

268	chezmoi apply         # Apply config files

275	## Keeping tools up-to-date
276	
277	`chezmoi apply` is deliberately **install-only** — ansible roles mostly use
278	`state: present` / `creates:` idempotency so re-applying never silently bumps
279	every tool on your machine. For explicit upgrades, use the dedicated entry
280	points (see [`docs/this_repo/upgrades.md`](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) for the full matrix):
281	
282	```bash
283	just upgrade-all          # externals + brew + mise + uv + npm + cargo + dotnet + gem + agents + plugins
284	just upgrade-dry-run      # preview without executing
285	
286	# Per category (compose as you like):
287	just upgrade-brew         # formulas + casks (--greedy) + Brewfile (no --no-upgrade) + cleanup
288	just upgrade-mise         # mise self-update + `mise upgrade`
289	just upgrade-uv           # Python CLI tools (apprise, mlflow, sqlit-tui, ...)
290	just upgrade-npm          # global npm packages (Bitwarden CLI, readability-cli, ...)
291	just upgrade-cargo        # cargo install-update -a (bootstraps cargo-update)
292	just upgrade-dotnet       # .NET global tools (azure-cost-cli, ...)
293	just upgrade-gem          # Ruby gems (try-cli, tmuxinator, ...)
294	just upgrade-agents       # re-runs install.sh for Claude Code / OpenCode / Cursor CLI / Ollama / llmfit / RTK
295	just upgrade-plugins      # LazyVim :Lazy sync + TPM + claude-hud + pre-commit autoupdate + tldr + gh extensions
296	just upgrade-externals    # chezmoi upgrade + chezmoi apply --refresh-externals
297	```
298	
299	Underlying script: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) —
300	best-effort, prints a `SUCCESS / SKIPPED / FAILED` summary at the end. Full
301	docs, rationale, run-order diagram, and extension guide live in
302	[docs/this_repo/upgrades.md](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md).
303	
304	When installed, `just upgrade-plugins` also refreshes `claude-hud` to the
305	latest upstream release. Upstream `claude-hud` `v0.0.12+` now follows Claude
306	Code's official stdin `rate_limits` only, so the old credential-derived `Max`
307	plan badge may disappear after upgrade.
308	
309	## Multi-host apply (`just fleet-apply`)
310	
311	Push the same `chezmoi update --init` to every host in
312	`~/.config/fleet/machines.toml`, in parallel, with sudo password sourced from
313	plaintext / interactive prompt / Bitwarden CLI:
314	
315	```bash
316	just fleet-apply                     # parallel, all hosts (chezmoi update --init)
317	just fleet-apply-dry-run             # `chezmoi diff` on each host (no changes)
318	just fleet-apply-one lab-box         # single host, --serial mode (debug)
319	```
320	
321	Connection prefers `~/.ssh/config` aliases (`ProxyJump`, `IdentityAgent`,
322	etc. all inherited) and falls back to explicit `hostname/user/port/identity_file`.
323	Per-host log: `logs/fleet-apply/<UTC-timestamp>/<host>.log`. Exit code = number
324	of failed hosts. Inventory file is seeded once by chezmoi as a
325	`create_private_` template, so your edits are never overwritten.
326	
327	Conflict-handling defaults match the "push canonical config" mental model:
328	`--keep-going` is **on** (skip drifted files non-destructively, continue
329	the rest), `--force` is **off** (don't auto-overwrite). Pass
330	`--no-keep-going` to fail-fast, or `--force` to silently overwrite local
331	drift on the remote — see [docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md)
332	for the full flag reference and per-machine git override convention
333	(`~/.gitconfig.local`, same self-managed pattern as `~/.zshrc.adhoc`).
334	
335	## Testing
336	
337	Two layers, both opt-in — this is a personal dotfiles repo, tests only cover painful-regression zones:
338	
339	- **`just bats`** — fast unit tests (no Docker, no network). Covers proxy helpers (`tests/unit/zsh_proxy.bats`), `ghget` URL parsing (`tests/unit/ghget.bats`), and `lan-scan.sh` pure helpers (`tests/unit/lan_scan.bats`).
340	- **`just docker-test`** — smoke tests in a clean Ubuntu container: re-apply idempotency, zsh config parses, `oh-my-zsh` plugins present, core CLI tools on PATH, nested unit tests pass under Ubuntu zsh (`tests/smoke/docker_install.bats`).
341	- **`just check-all`** — everything: ansible syntax + pre-commit + `bats` + `docker-test`.
342	
343	`shellcheck` and `shfmt` run via pre-commit on `scripts/*.sh` (see `.pre-commit-config.yaml`).
344	
345	## Docker Testing

349	just docker-test
350

352	just docker-run
353	
354	# Build specific profiles

356	just docker-china      # China mirror profile
357	```

<summary>Tool use: **Write**</summary>

```tmpl
# ~/.zlogin - login-shell hooks (managed by chezmoi)
# Prints an SSH-only MOTD banner. Local terminals get nothing.
#
# Trigger conditions (all 4 must hold):
#   1. $SSH_CONNECTION non-empty (i.e. you SSH'd in)
#   2. stdout is a TTY (filters `ssh host 'cmd'`, scp, rsync, fleet-apply)
#   3. not inside tmux (banner is once-per-SSH-session, not per-pane)
#   4. MOTD_DISABLE != 1 (taste-based opt-out via ~/.zshrc.adhoc)
#
# Tools: figlet (apt + brew, installed by ansible devtools role).
# Falls back to plain `== hostname ==` on first boot before figlet exists.

[ -n "$SSH_CONNECTION" ] || return 0
[ -t 1 ] || return 0
[ -z "$TMUX" ] || return 0
[ "${MOTD_DISABLE:-0}" = "1" ] && return 0

_motd_host="$(hostname -s 2>/dev/null || hostname)"
_motd_cols="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 80)}"

printf '\033[36m'
if command -v figlet >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    figlet -w "$_motd_cols" -f small -- "$_motd_host" 2>/dev/null \
        || figlet -w "$_motd_cols" -- "$_motd_host" 2>/dev/null \
        || printf '== %s ==\n' "$_motd_host"
else
    printf '== %s ==\n' "$_motd_host"
fi
printf '\033[0m'

_motd_profile='{{ .profile }}'
_motd_os="$(uname -sr)"
_motd_up="$(uptime 2>/dev/null | sed -E 's/.*up *([^,]+),.*/\1/' | xargs)"
_motd_ip="$(echo "$SSH_CONNECTION" | awk '{print $3}')"

printf '\033[2m'
printf 'profile=%s  os=%s  up=%s  via=%s\n' \
    "$_motd_profile" "$_motd_os" "${_motd_up:-?}" "${_motd_ip:-?}"
printf '\033[0m\n'

unset _motd_host _motd_cols _motd_profile _motd_os _motd_up _motd_ip

```

```

```md
# SSH login banner (MOTD)

A short login-shell hook that prints a big `figlet`-style hostname banner plus a one-line metadata row when you SSH into a managed host. Local terminals stay silent — the banner exists purely for **fleet identification**: when you `ssh` to one of ten boxes managed by [`just fleet-apply`](../this_repo/fleet-apply.md), the banner answers "which box am I on?" instantly.

Source: [`dot_zlogin.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_zlogin.tmpl) → `~/.zlogin`.

## What it looks like

\```
   _   _      _    ___  _
  | | | |__ _| |__|__ \| |__
  | |_| / _` | '_ \ / // '_ \
   \___/\__,_|_.__//_(_)_.__/

profile=ubuntu_server  os=Linux 6.5.0-21-generic  up=4 days  via=192.168.1.42
\```

(font: `figlet -f small`. Cyan banner, dim metadata row.)

## Trigger conditions

The banner fires only when **all four** gates pass:

| # | Gate | Why |
|---|------|-----|
| 1 | `[ -n "$SSH_CONNECTION" ]` | The core trigger — empty on console / local / `tmux new` |
| 2 | `[ -t 1 ]` | stdout must be a TTY → suppresses `ssh host 'cmd'`, `scp`, `rsync`, and the chezmoi `fleet-apply` SSH probes |
| 3 | `[ -z "$TMUX" ]` | Print once per SSH session, not per tmux pane |
| 4 | `[ "${MOTD_DISABLE:-0}" != "1" ]` | Taste-based runtime opt-out |

zsh sources `.zlogin` only for **login shells**. New tmux panes (default config) and non-interactive `zsh -c` invocations don't even reach the script — gate 2 + 3 are belt-and-suspenders against tmux configs that force login shells.

## Tools used

`figlet` is installed by the ansible `devtools` role (apt + brew). The companion utilities `toilet` (color/Unicode figlet superset) and `lolcat` (rainbow color filter) are installed too but **not used by the MOTD itself** — they're general-purpose user CLIs you can pipe to:

\```sh
echo "deploy ok" | toilet -f mono12 --metal
fortune | cowsay | lolcat        # if you also install cowsay/fortune
\```

The MOTD uses only ANSI escapes (cyan + dim) so it stays deterministic over flaky SSH and never depends on a separate color filter being installed.

## Opt out

Add to `~/.zshrc.adhoc` (auto-created by [`dot_zshrc.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_zshrc.tmpl)):

\```sh
export MOTD_DISABLE=1
\```

This survives `chezmoi apply` because `~/.zshrc.adhoc` is not chezmoi-managed.

## First boot (before figlet is installed)

Chezmoi deploys `~/.zlogin` before the ansible `devtools` role runs. If you SSH in during that window:

- `command -v figlet` returns false
- Falls back to plain `== <hostname> ==`
- Metadata line still prints

After ansible finishes, the next SSH login uses figlet.

## Customization

### Change the figlet font

Edit `~/.zlogin` (or the source `dot_zlogin.tmpl` if you want the change to roll through chezmoi to all your machines):

\```sh
figlet -w "$_motd_cols" -f banner -- "$_motd_host"     # blocky banner font
figlet -w "$_motd_cols" -f slant -- "$_motd_host"      # italic slant
figlet -w "$_motd_cols" -f standard -- "$_motd_host"   # default (taller)
\```

`figlet -f` followed by Tab in a shell with `figlet` installed lists all available fonts under `/usr/share/figlet/` (Linux) or `$(brew --prefix figlet)/share/figlet/fonts/` (macOS). The `small` default is chosen because it fits inside a ~24-row mobile SSH window without wrapping for hostnames up to ~20 chars.

### Show FQDN instead of short hostname

\```sh
_motd_host="$(hostname -f 2>/dev/null || hostname)"
\```

Caveat: long FQDNs may wrap even with `-f small`; consider `-f mini` if so.

### Skip the metadata row

Delete the second `printf` block (`profile=… os=… up=… via=…`).

### Use `toilet` for color gradients

`toilet` is a figlet superset with built-in gradients. Replace the figlet block with:

\```sh
toilet -w "$_motd_cols" -f small --gay -- "$_motd_host"
\```

Tradeoff: `--gay`/`--metal` palettes are pretty over a clean SSH session but can look mangled on terminals without 256-color support. The current ANSI-cyan default is more conservative.

## Why not `/etc/motd` or PAM `motd.dynamic`?

System MOTD lives in `/etc/motd` or `/etc/update-motd.d/*` and applies to **every** user. This banner is per-user, lives in the dotfiles repo, and respects user opt-out — no root needed, no impact on other accounts. Ubuntu's default MOTD news / advertisements remain a separate concern (silence them via `touch ~/.hushlogin` or `chmod -x /etc/update-motd.d/50-motd-news`).

## Related

- [`dot_zlogin.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_zlogin.tmpl) — the source template
- [`dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml) — installs `figlet`, `toilet`, `lolcat`
- [`dot_zshrc.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_zshrc.tmpl) — auto-creates `~/.zshrc.adhoc` (where `MOTD_DISABLE=1` lives)
- [Fleet apply](../this_repo/fleet-apply.md) — the multi-host workflow this banner is most useful for

```

對,不會掛掉 — 而且我可以直接驗證給你看。

## 為什麼不會掛

`dot_zlogin.tmpl` 對 `figlet` 有明確的 `command -v` 檢查 + fallback:

```sh
if command -v figlet >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    figlet -w "$_motd_cols" -f small -- "$_motd_host" 2>/dev/null \
        || figlet -w "$_motd_cols" -- "$_motd_host" 2>/dev/null \
        || printf '== %s ==\n' "$_motd_host"
else
    printf '== %s ==\n' "$_motd_host"   # ← 完全沒裝 figlet 走這條
fi
```

而且 — **`toilet` 跟 `lolcat` `.zlogin` 根本沒用到**,它們純粹是裝給你 user 自己玩的 utility。

其他用到的工具都是 POSIX 標準必有的:`hostname` / `tput`(有 `|| echo 80` 兜底)/ `uname` / `uptime` / `sed` / `awk` / `xargs` / `printf`,而且每個外部呼叫都有 `2>/dev/null` 抑制錯誤訊息。

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-06 07:44:24Z)**_

回答兩個問題:

## 1. 不會蓋掉 Ubuntu 的系統 MOTD

它們是**完全分開的兩層**,會疊著顯示:

```
SSH 連入
 ↓
PAM 認證 → pam_motd.so 印 /etc/motd + /etc/update-motd.d/* 的輸出  ← Ubuntu 那串
 ↓
sshd 啟動 user 的 login shell
 ↓
zsh: .zshenv → .zprofile → .zshrc → .zlogin                         ← 我們的 figlet
 ↓
prompt 出現
```

| 層級 | 來源 | 範圍 | 我們動了嗎 |
|------|------|------|----------|
| 系統 MOTD | `/etc/motd` + `/etc/update-motd.d/*` | 所有使用者(系統管) | ❌ 完全沒碰 |
| 我們的 banner | `~/.zlogin`(per-user,chezmoi 管) | 只有當前帳號 | ✅ 新增 |

所以 SSH 上去你會先看到 Ubuntu 那串(load average / 待更新數量 / 廣告...),然後我們的 figlet 跟 metadata。

如果你覺得 Ubuntu 那串太囉嗦想關掉:

```bash
touch ~/.hushlogin                          # 關 pam_motd 對你個人(不影響別人)
sudo chmod -x /etc/update-motd.d/50-motd-news  # 系統層,關 Canonical 廣告
```

但這是另一回事,不在這次改動範圍。要的話我可以另外做(可以加進 ansible 的 `zsh` 或新建 role)。
